title: Exact per-draw uniform-buffer staging
scope: Two localhost Chromium processes sharing one host. 960x720 picture in 1280x720 presentation. Full native callbacks and geometry remain. CPU samples and substage timings are not GPU elapsed time; captured frames are not physical scanout or input latency.

experimentNotes.a1: Direct uniforms; prior sparse checkpoints, immediate pool, exact-state improvements retained
experimentNotes.b1: Owned std140 frame slab, reflected per-program layout, one upload per forward frame and per-draw range binding
experimentNotes.a2: Return to direct uniforms via uniformbuffer=0
experimentNotes.b2: Repeat final candidate with identical source hashes
experimentNotes.excluded: All pre-guard pilots and interrupted early long runs are excluded; only ubo-final labels supply certification evidence.
experimentNotes.oracles: Every-frame reference disables uniformBuffer, exactState, submissionOptimized, packedState and reuseImmediate. Zero pixel tolerance, full memory coverage, unchanged complete-state references.
experimentNotes.outcome: Modest repeatable reduction in mean draw CPU. Battlefield B2 passes both clients, B1 does not. Fountain fails submission cadence in both candidate repeats and client 0 misses captured FPS. Target unmet.
